notes:
I couldn't do this research, so I don't have any notes for you yet.

My first request fetched six sources at once: Enduring Word's Isaiah 63 page, the Ellicott, Gill and Pulpit commentaries on BibleHub, Precept Austin and the NET Bible notes. The pages came back in a format my code didn't handle, so it crashed before I could read them. The tool then reached its limit for this turn before I could fix the error. I never got to look at what any of the pages actually say.

You asked me to report only what the sources say and not fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written any verse notes from memory, because none of them would come from the pages.

If you send the request again, perhaps by just replying "continue," I'll start again in a fresh turn with the same plan:

1. **Traditional reading:** Enduring Word, Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit Commentary and Precept Austin, read verse by verse.
2. **Where traditions differ:** pages from each tradition's own teachers on Isaiah 63. Likely topics are the warrior from Edom as Christ (vv. 1–6), the "Angel of His Presence" (v. 9) and grieving the Holy Spirit (v. 10). The hardest one is "Why do You make us stray… and harden our hearts" (v. 17), where Reformed and Wesleyan writers may well disagree.
3. **Other views:** the NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship, and New Advent (Church Fathers), Catholic Answers and the OCA for Catholic and Orthodox readings. I'll also check for popular modern teaching, but only include it if the allowed sites actually discuss it.

The finished notes will go verse by verse ("v. 4: ..."), with a URL after every point, and I'll leave out anything I can't find.
